blockers.what: The win32 branch of archivePlan is never executed with its own command: the test runs execFileSync('tar', plan.args) from PATH instead of plan.command (the System32 full path), and is skipped whenever the first tar on PATH is not bsdtar. On a Windows runner whose PATH puts Git's GNU tar first, the only test of the Windows zip silently skips, which is the exact case the full path exists for. (tools/archive.test.ts:27, tools/archive.test.ts:59-63, found by the `unit` tier)

The new tests create temporary directories and directory symlinks/junctions with mkdtempSync and never remove them (no afterAll/rmSync). (tools/python.test.ts:77,98; tools/bin.test.ts:121; tools/archive.test.ts:18,51,61; tools/find-firefox.test.ts:16; tools/is-main.test.ts:18,29,36, found by the `unit` tier)
The declaration comment for PYTHON3_CHECK still says 'Exits 0 only under Python 3.' while the implementation and its JSDoc require 3.7 or later. (tools/python.d.mts:6, found by the `unit` tier)

The Windows CI job is the only proof that B-162 and B-163 hold on Windows, and nothing guards its step list. tools/ci.test.ts reads the whole workflow as one text ('runs every gate the local chain runs', 'starts Python only through tools/python.mjs'), so the Linux job alone satisfies it. Removing pnpm ux:lint or package:check from 'gates (windows)' would keep every test green (.github/workflows/ci.yml:102-131 (job windows), tools/ci.test.ts:86, found by the `seam` tier)

The feed tools keep a second way of spawning pnpm that did not get binInvocation: runBounded('pnpm', ...) without a shell. On Windows that is EINVAL. It is documented as unsupported (runbook 'Windows' table: the feed tools do not work on Windows), but no test or guard refuses running them there (tools/feed-job.mjs:298, tools/feed/bootstrap.mjs:191, tools/install-feed-agent.mjs:173, tools/publish-feed.mjs:189, found by the `seam` tier)

The main-module rule has two implementations: tools/is-main.mjs (realpath of both sides) and apps/mail-cli/src/entry.ts isEntry (realpath of argv[1], case folding on win32, extensionless match). is-main.mjs calls itself 'the one implementation'. They agree on every case the suites exercise today, and the mail command does not depend on isEntry (apps/mail-cli/src/entry.ts:35, tools/is-main.mjs:17, found by the `seam` tier)

geckodriver started through npx outlives the Firefox run on Linux and macOS. endTree ends the whole tree only on win32; on POSIX it is child.kill() of npx, as before. The runner reaped an orphan geckodriver after the job in this run (40665996073, e2e firefox: 'Terminate orphan process ... geckodriver-0.37.1') and on main (40402594155). Not moved by this change, but endTree is the place that now owns it (tools/firefox-e2e.mjs:155,180,475 via tools/bin.mjs endTree, found by the `seam` tier)

The engines range narrowed to ^22.18.0 || >=23.6.0. The feed agent runs pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --filter @okolos/proxy under whatever node the login shell resolves (plist line 74), and neither the installer nor the bootstrap checks that node against the floor. If pnpm refuses a root project whose engines do not match, a machine on node 22.0 to 22.17 or 23.0 to 23.5 now fails at the install stage when the lockfile moves. This Mac runs v26.10.0, so the risk is to other machines (tools/feed-job.mjs:298, tools/feed/bootstrap.mjs:191, tools/launchd/app.okolos.feed.plist:74, found by the `seam` tier)
